q: The Coding Theorem (Levin's theorem) for the universal semi-measure m states that for any computable semi-measure P:
opts: m(x) ≥ c_P · P(x) for some constant c_P > 0 independent of x (m dominates all computable semi-measures)
m = P for the natural measure
exp: Levin's coding theorem: m(x) = 2^{-K(x)} up to constants, and m dominates every computable (semi-)measure: m(x) ≥ c_P · P(x). This makes m the 'universal a priori probability': it assigns at least as much probability as any computable model, up to a constant factor.
